name: Christian nationalism
description: A tradition seeking national public identity and civil institutions grounded in Christianity, assessed separately from personal Christian belief and from clerical government.

axes.brief: Civil leadership serves a Christian national common good and may retain representative constitutional institutions.
axes.counterEvidence: Versions differ on pluralist equality and strong executive leadership; Christian identity alone does not establish military rule.

qualifications.5: Constitutional competition and limiting an anti-Christian political programme compete.

axes.brief: Public moral order qualifies individual choice while political and religious speech rights retain importance.
axes.counterEvidence: Opposition to secular state intrusion coexists with moral regulation; health, preventive policing and firearms are low-confidence extensions.

axes.brief: A shared Christian national culture is prioritised over competing public cultural foundations.
axes.counterEvidence: Private communities may retain customs; Christian public identity is not necessarily a biological racial exclusion.

axes.brief: Cultural continuity and bounded national responsibilities favour controlled admission and integration.
axes.counterEvidence: Christian hospitality and family obligations qualify blanket exclusion of every refugee or foreign worker.

axes.brief: National security and protection of community coexist with restraint toward foreign nation-building.
axes.counterEvidence: The doctrine does not prescribe one military budget or target-selection code; protective force differs from perpetual conquest.

axes.brief: The national Christian community should govern itself rather than submit to a universal secular political order.
axes.counterEvidence: Cooperation with other nations remains possible without common supreme political authority.

axes.brief: Family property and private enterprise coexist with public institutions serving the national common good.
axes.counterEvidence: Christian nationalism does not determine utility or banking ownership; economic answers are scoped contemporary conservative estimates.

qualifications.8: Private finance and public community provision compete.

axes.brief: National productive resilience and selected trade coexist under national community obligations.
axes.counterEvidence: The public-identity doctrine does not prescribe a universal tariff schedule; market-oriented and protectionist factions coexist.

axes.brief: Routine enterprise choice is retained with targeted intervention for national and family purposes.
axes.counterEvidence: No comprehensive production plan follows from Christianity; central monetary and wage mechanisms are contextual estimates.

axes.brief: Family responsibility, property and community welfare favour a safety net with work and local obligations.
axes.counterEvidence: Christian care for the poor qualifies simple tax minimisation; political variants differ greatly on redistribution.

axes.brief: Christian national foundations and public moral formation should shape law, education and official recognition.
axes.counterEvidence: Civil magistracy remains distinct from clerical supremacy; denominational differences qualify compulsory religious court authority.

axes.brief: Christian family and moral traditions guide public sex, marriage and educational norms.
axes.counterEvidence: Particular traditions differ on abortion exceptions, parental authority and legal coercion; the scope is contemporary conservative Christian-national politics.

axes.brief: Productive development is valuable while moral limits and bodily integrity constrain enhancement.
axes.counterEvidence: Not all Christian nationalists reject biotechnology; doctrine does not specify every AI or ecological safety threshold.

axes.brief: Local community and family leadership coexist with national protection of Christian public institutions.
axes.counterEvidence: Localism is not an unlimited right to secede or overturn the national moral settlement.

axes.brief: Moral education shapes conduct while created human nature and sex differences also matter.
axes.counterEvidence: Christian public identity does not entail inherited racial crime or IQ explanations; those are rejected as the less-supported interpretation.

qualifications.8: Moral formation and individual predisposition both shape empathy.

phrase: A society where national institutions preserve a Christian public identity and civil government promotes the community’s Christian moral foundations.

religion.reason: This profile explicitly represents a Christian political tradition; the faith-specific comparison prerequisite is Christian identity, not a claim that every survey sympathiser is religious.
